notes: I couldn't open the PDFs directly. WebFetch returned the PDF as compressed binary, and the Read tool needs poppler, which isn't installed. Bash and PowerShell are disabled, so I couldn't extract the text. The figures below come from a web-search summary of the monitor, not from a page I read, so I have no page numbers. I did not get absolute NIPT counts for 2021-2024 or any 2025 figure. 2025 data is not expected before around Jan 2027. Only the 2024 pregnancy denominator (171,349) is confirmed. Uptake in the Netherlands was 51.2% in 2020, 67.8% in 2023 and 73.5% in 2024, with the abnormal rate flat at 0.5%. That is still growth, with no flattening yet. The 2024 monitor is the first year at 73.5%, so it can't show a plateau on its own. A plateau would show up only in the 2025 monitor.
how_to_mine: Download the PDFs (pns.nl 2026-01 monitor-2024-prenatal-screening-nipt-and-structural-ultrasound-scan.pdf, monitor-2024-nipt-seo.pdf, professionalsmonitor-2024-nipt-seo.pdf) and the 2023 monitor (pns.nl 2025-01/20250109_Monitor prenatale screening 2023.pdf). Extract the text with pdftotext or pypdf in an environment where Bash or Python is allowed. Pull the NIPT uptake tables for 2021-2024, the number of pregnancies per year, and the regional spread. Then compute absolute NIPT counts as uptake times pregnancies (about 126K in 2024 if 73.5% of 171,349 is right). Compare against the 13-week scan uptake of 79.8%. Check the Kamerbrieven 2026D03959 and 2026D06644 for 2025 interim figures.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Dutch national NIPT uptake is already 73.5% of pregnancies, near the 79.8% scan ceiling, which limits future NIPT volume growth.
items.detail: Under the Dutch screening programme (Peridos registry), NIPT uptake was 51.2% in 2020, 67.8% in 2023 and 73.5% in 2024, from 171,349 pregnancies. Abnormal results stayed at 0.5%. Uptake of the 13-week scan was 79.8% and the 20-week scan 86.9%. NIPT uptake is therefore about 6 points below the 13-week scan. Annual uptake gains slowed from about +5.6 points a year (2020-23) to +5.7 points in 2024, so there is no flattening yet. The 2025 monitor is the test of whether it has plateaued. This is a summary from search results; I did not read the PDF pages.
items.source_name: RIVM / PNS NIPT Monitor 2024 (IQ Health, Radboudumc; Peridos registry)

items.why_new: This is a national NIPT uptake series, with uptake already high in a universal-access country. Nothing like it is in the exclusion list.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Dutch NIPT uptake was still rising in 2024, up 5.7 points from 2023, so NIPT volume had not yet plateaued.
items.detail: Uptake rose from 67.8% in 2023 to 73.5% in 2024, a relative gain of about 8%, and from 51.2% in 2020. Counselling was registered in 94.9% of pregnancies, against 93.6% in 2023. A plateau is not proven until the 2025 data, which is expected around Jan 2027. This is the watch-out for the NIPT-maturing argument.
items.why_new: This is a quantified counterpoint from a national registry, which the known list lacks.
